Tooltip_BB_Bowie_Military: Government-issue fighting knife. Heavy, plain and built to last.
Tooltip_BB_Bowie_Sporting: A good hunting knife from the counter of a Kentucky gun store.
Tooltip_BB_Bowie_Knockoff: Cheap import from a flea market table. Dulls fast and wears out faster.
Tooltip_BB_Bowie_Handmade: Forged and fitted by hand. Rough, but it holds up.
Tooltip_BB_Fillet_Sporting: Thin, flexible blade for cleaning fish. A step above the bait shop kind.
Tooltip_BB_Fillet_Knockoff: Bait shop special. Thin steel that won't stay sharp long.
Tooltip_BB_Fillet_Handmade: Forged from scrap steel and wrapped in leather. Does the job.
Tooltip_BB_Folder_Military: Issued lockback folder. The blade locks open and stays put.
Tooltip_BB_Folder_Sporting: Lockback folder from a sporting goods store. Fits any pocket.
Tooltip_BB_Folder_Knockoff: Cheap folder with a loose lock. Better than nothing.
Tooltip_BB_Trapper_Sporting: Two-blade slip-joint, the kind every grandfather in Kentucky carried.
Tooltip_BB_Trapper_Knockoff: Gas station pocketknife. Soft steel, wobbly blades.
Tooltip_BB_Balisong_Sporting: Butterfly knife. Popular with collectors and teenagers since the movies.
Tooltip_BB_Balisong_Knockoff: Cheap butterfly knife from a mall kiosk. The pins rattle.
Tooltip_BB_Blade_Unfinished: A forged blade without a handle. Needs to be assembled and sharpened.
